title: Intervening at Model Output with Uncertainty Flags: Does Appending Confidence Reduce User Overreliance?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The core finding that verbalized uncertainty influences user reliance has been established by multiple user studies (ScienceDirect 2025, ICLR 2024, Nature MI 2024). The nuanced finding that medium uncertainty is optimal is already documented. Limited incremental value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires a user study to measure whether flags reduce reliance. Same IRB and recruitment challenges as gen-0787. The model-side implementation (appending flags) is trivial, but the evaluation requires human participants.

narrow_scope.reasoning: User study component makes this broad. Even a small-scale vignette study with stated reliance is substantial. Could be scoped to just measuring whether models produce different confidence levels on sycophantic vs. honest responses (no user study), but as stated includes user evaluation.

novelty.reasoning: This has been extensively studied. 'Confronting verbalized uncertainty' (ScienceDirect 2025) directly measures how LLM verbalized uncertainty influences users in AI-assisted decision-making, finding that medium uncertainty maximizes trust while high uncertainty causes distrust. 'Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?' (ICLR 2024) evaluates confidence elicitation methods. 'What large language models know and what people think they know' (Nature Machine Intelligence 2024) examines the gap between LLM accuracy and user perception. The core research question (do confidence flags reduce user overreliance?) has been answered: yes, but with nuanced effects depending on confidence level calibration.
